title: token-breakdown-ux-alternatives-and-backlog
content:
Purpose:
Small exploratory doc capturing several distinct wireframe directions and a prioritized grooming backlog for a token-level cost + latency breakdown dashboard. Intended audience: Console PM, Design, Eng leads (hosting + dedicated), SRE for observability hooks. This is a working doc — rough sketches, open questions, and discrete grooming tasks.

Context / problem statement:
- Customers and internal SREs need easy answers to: which routes, model variants, and prompt patterns drive the majority of token spend and tail latency.
- Existing console shows aggregated per-route latency and cost, but it's hard to slice tokens by generation vs prompt vs cached prefixes, or by model variant quantization.
- Goal: create a token-aware breakdown view that helps teams reduce unit cost without blindly turning on destructive optimizations.

High-level requirements (non-exhaustive):
1) Show token spend and latency distributions at three granularities: route (API path), model variant (e.g., 13B-8bit, 70B-16bit), and prompt-template (user-defined groups).
2) Distinguish tokens consumed for prompt vs generation vs retry/fallback vs cached hits.
3) Allow timeframe and cohort filtering (region, customer tier/dedicated vs hosted, http status).
4) Surface recommendations: batching suggestions, quantization tradeoffs, KV-cache hit opportunities, and cost delta estimates for each recommendation.
5) Integrate with rollouts: see which model versions cause regressions in latency/cost and enable quick rollback links.

Wireframe directions (three alternatives)

A — Waterfall Token Flow (preferred for engineering)
- Overview: vertical waterfall showing tokens entering the system left-to-right: incoming prompt tokens -> prefix cache hit/miss split -> generation tokens -> post-processing tokens -> retries/fallbacks. Each stage shows median and p99 latency and token counts.
- UI elements: stacked bars (token counts) with overlaid latency sparkline; selectable model variant toggles above; row per route in a collapsible list.
- Interactions: hover shows sample traces (trace id link to tracing UI), click expands to sample requests and prompt hash.
- Pros: clear causal view (where tokens are spent), maps well to runtime internals.
- Cons: might be dense for non-engr users; needs backend to tag token-type per request.

B — Sankey by Cost & Latency (better for executives/product)
- Overview: Sankey diagram where flows represent token volume weighted by cost; nodes are route/model/prompt-group/caching. Latency is encoded by color (cool -> warm), with thickness mapped to token spend.
- UI elements: zoomable canvas, legend showing color->latency ranges, tooltip includes estimated $ cost for flow.
- Interactions: drag to group nodes, search prompts by name, pin model variant comparisons.
- Pros: very visual, communicates cost hotspots at glance.
- Cons: heavy on client rendering; accessibility concerns.

C — Table-first with Inline Visuals (balanced approach)
- Overview: prioritized table of hot routes (sorted by token spend delta week-over-week). Columns: route, model variant, tokens (prompt/gen/cache), cost estimate, median latency, p95 latency, suggested action (e.g., enable caching, reduce max_tokens, switch to 8-bit variant). Each row expands to show a small inline sparkline + micro-waterfall.
- UI elements: filters at top, bulk select to apply recommendations to multiple routes, CTA to open a rollout canary.
- Pros: aligns with customer workflows (ops triage), easy to implement iteratively.
- Cons: less visual than Sankey; may hide systemic interactions between routes.

Data model and telemetry needs (engineering input required)
- Required telemetry fields per request: route_id, model_variant, prompt_template_id (or hash), tokens_prompt, tokens_generated, tokens_cached, tokens_retry, request_latency_ms, stage_latencies (decode_ms, prep_ms, post_ms), request_timestamp, region, customer_tier, project_id, trace_id, response_status.
- Aggregation: hourly rollups plus raw-sample retention for 7 days; support rollup by route/model/prompt-template.
- Backend compute: cost estimates require model-specific unit price table (hosted and dedicated multipliers). Cache hit accounting must be per-prefix key; confirm current prefix metrics exist in infra.
- Open questions for infra: do we currently persist tokens_generated per request? SRE says we have token counts in runtime logs but need ingestion to metrics pipeline (INF-telemetry).

Privacy and data controls:
- For private deployments, we must honor telemetry opt-outs; offer masked prompt hashes and only surface prompt template names where customer allowed.
- Add a toggle for "show sample prompt text" which requires a privacy opt-in.

Backlog grooming (prioritized)
- P0 (must ship MVP within 6 sprints):
  - (UX) Implement Table-first layout + row expansion (Direction C) — ticket UX-517.
  - (Eng) Add tokens_prompt and tokens_generated to telemetry ingestion pipeline — ticket INF-3421.
  - (SRE) Create hourly aggregations and a cached rollup view for console to query — ticket SRE-2145.
  - (Product) Define model-unit cost table and per-variant multipliers for hosted vs dedicated — ticket PRD-196.
- P1 (next 3 sprints):
  - (UX) Add micro-waterfall cell visualization to expanded rows.
  - (Data) Implement cohort filters (region, tier, project).
  - (Eng) Build sample-trace linking to tracing UI (requires trace_id in telemetry).
- P2 (later/experimental):
  - (Design) Prototype Sankey cost flow canvas for executive mode.
  - (ML/Infra) Instrument KV-cache hit/miss ratio per prompt-prefix.
  - (Product) Auto-recommendations engine: batching, quantization, cache suggestions.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Console page lists top 30 routes by token spend with tokens split into prompt/gen/cache columns.
- Each route row shows median and p95 latency and an estimated $/day contribution.
- Row expansion shows 3 sample requests (masked) and trace links.
- Filters for timeframe and region work and match SLO dashboards.
- Backend metrics ingestion latency < 15 minutes for hourly rollups.

Design notes / microcopy ideas:
- Header: "Token Economics — where your tokens go and what they cost"
- Badges: "High spend", "P99 latency regression", "Cache opportunity"
- Recommendation CTA example: "Try 8-bit variant (est. -22% cost) — create canary"
- Tooltip for cost: explain "Estimated $ = token_count * model_unit_rate * region_multiplier — excludes infra overhead and enterprise discounts"

Open questions / decisions required:
- Should the console expose raw prompt text by default? (Security/legal: no.)
- Do we show per-customer/token costs in hosted for multi-tenant customers? (Need legal approval.)
- How to attribute tokens from function calls / tool calling flows? Need runtime to emit tool-call token split.

Quick implementation plan (first 3 sprints):
Sprint 1:
  - UX: detailed table mockups; create tiny design system components (micro-waterfall SVG); two interactive rows in Figma.
  - Eng: schema for telemetry additions, implement ingestion for tokens_prompt/tokens_generated in staging.
  - Data: define hourly aggregation schema and costing materialized views.
Sprint 2:
  - UX: finalize table-first interaction patterns, accessibility audit.
  - Eng: backend rollups and REST endpoint (paginated) for console, sample-trace linking.
  - Product: ship initial model-unit cost table, connect to backend.
Sprint 3:
  - UI: implement row expansion, inline visuals, filters, and bulk action CTA.
  - QA: run synthetic traffic to validate numbers vs ground-truth logs.

Notes to self (todo before next sync with design):
- Check with infra whether trace_id is guaranteed for cached responses (Samir).
- Get legal signoff draft for prompt masking options (Greta).
- Draft copy for recommendation modals and rollback confirmation (Jonah).
- Prepare 5-minute demo showing how to reduce spend by 15% using batching + cache in a dedicated tenant.

Appendix — example API responses for console (mock)
- GET /api/console/token-breakdown?start=2026-02-01T00:00Z&end=2026-02-07T00:00Z&group_by=route&page=1
- mock response (rows):
  - route: "/v1/generate/chat", model_variant: "rw-13b-8bit", tokens_prompt: "1,432,213", tokens_gen: "3,112,901", tokens_cache: "512,102", est_cost_usd: "$412.23", median_ms: "85", p95_ms: "380", suggestions: "enable-prefix-cache"

Final thoughts:
- Recommendation: start with Table-first (C) — fastest path to value and easiest to iterate. Collect telemetry in parallel for richer visual prototypes (A/B).
- Keep the early UX focused on actionable rows and CTAs (create canary / suggest batch) rather than perfect visualizations.

Draft owners: Maya Chen (PM), Samir Patel (Eng owner), Greta Müller (Legal), Jonah Park (Design)
summary: Working doc: three wireframe directions (waterfall, sankey, table-first), telemetry needs, prioritized backlog P0/P1/P2, MVP acceptance criteria, sprint plan, open questions
